home.heroText: Practice real workplace and everyday moments through scenarios, and build your active bystander skills.
home.aboutLead:
An active bystander is someone who, when they witness a discriminatory comment or behavior, doesn't look away — and steps in, in some form.
You don't need to make a big scene. A quick word in the moment, or just checking in afterward, can mean a lot to the person it happened to.

frameworkPreview.distract: Change the subject to ease the tension
frameworkPreview.delegate: Bring in someone better placed to help
frameworkPreview.document: Keep a record of what happened
frameworkPreview.delay: Check in with them one-on-one, later
frameworkPreview.direct: Say something, right in the moment

home.roleplayTitle: Why this roleplay — and how to use it
home.roleplayLead: In-the-moment judgment calls are harder than they sound. Thinking through "what would I actually do?" ahead of time makes it easier to act when it counts.

choose.title: Pick a scenario
choose.body: Choose a single situation that resonates with you, or hit "Take the 5-question check" for five scenarios back-to-back.

answer.title: Decide what you'd do
answer.body: Pick from four options, then write a quick line in your own words.

reflect.title: See the feedback
reflect.body: See how that choice tends to land, and how other people answered — then carry it forward.

home.scenarioPickerLead: Pick one situation and take your time thinking through what you'd actually do.

scenario.chooseAction: In this situation, how would you step in?
scenario.notRecommended: That reaction makes sense — here's a further step
scenario.strategyIntro: This is the “{strategy}” move in active bystander intervention
scenario.frameworkIntro: There's more than one valid way to intervene. Choose based on the situation and your own safety.
scenario.yourNextMove: Here's how they responded. What would you say or do next?

reactionExplain.defensive: When called out, people sometimes react defensively without quite meaning to — it's an almost automatic way of protecting themselves. This person seems to be doing just that.
reactionExplain.confused: Sometimes people genuinely don't register what the problem was, even once it's pointed out. This person seems to be caught in that kind of confusion.
reactionExplain.reflective: Some people are able to take a correction in stride and reflect on what they said. This person seems to be doing that.

scenario.impressionPrompt: Watching this play out, how did it make you feel?
scenario.reasoningPrompt: Why did you decide to do that?
scenario.documentPrompt: What would you record, and how would you follow up?
scenario.delegatePrompt: Who would you raise this with, and how?
scenario.laterFollowUpPrompt: If you brought this up with them afterward, what would you say?

intro.title: Before you start
intro.lead: An active bystander is someone who, when they witness discriminatory comments or behavior, doesn't look away — they respond in some way.
intro.purpose: This roleplay walks you through 5 scenarios and asks how you'd respond if you were actually there.
intro.emphasis: This isn't about guessing the "right" answer. Take a moment with each scene and think through what you'd realistically do.
